q: In 1982 Argentina's military junta invaded these islands off its coast. Britain sent a task force under Margaret Thatcher and retook them in about ten weeks. The islands are called the Malvinas in Spanish. For 10 points, name these islands.

This Scottish-born politician became the first prime minister of Canada after Confederation in 1867. He pushed the Canadian Pacific Railway to its completion. For 10 points, name this Conservative leader, who has the initials J.A.

This Metis leader led the Red River Rebellion in 1869 and the North-West Rebellion in 1885. He founded a provisional government in what is now Manitoba. He was hanged for treason. For 10 points, name this Canadian figure.

In April 1917 four Canadian divisions fought together for the first time and captured a ridge in northern France. It is remembered as a defining moment for Canadian national identity. For 10 points, name this World War I battle, commemorated by a monument.

In 1915 Australian and New Zealand troops landed at a cove on a peninsula in Turkey, in a campaign planned by Winston Churchill. The Allied operation failed and the troops were evacuated. For 10 points, name this campaign, commemorated each April on Anzac Day.

This French explorer founded a settlement on the Saint Lawrence River in 1608 at the site of present-day Quebec City. He explored the Great Lakes region and a lake in New York now bearing his name. He allied with the Huron against the Iroquois. For 10 points, name this "Father of New France."

In 1610 this English explorer sailed into a large bay in northern Canada, searching for a Northwest Passage. His crew mutinied and left him adrift in a small boat. A river and a bay in North America are named for him. For 10 points, name this man.

In 1845 two ships named Erebus and Terror left England to find the Northwest Passage and disappeared. The commander was a Royal Navy officer, and search parties later found evidence of cannibalism. For 10 points, name this lost expedition led by Sir John.

This Anglo-Irish explorer's ship Endurance was crushed by ice in the Weddell Sea in 1915. He and his men survived on Elephant Island, and he sailed for help to South Georgia. For 10 points, name this Antarctic explorer.

This British naturalist sailed aboard HMS Beagle from 1831 to 1836 and studied finches in the Galapagos Islands. His 1859 book proposed natural selection. For 10 points, name this scientist who wrote On the Origin of Species.

This secret American project during World War II, directed by J. Robert Oppenheimer at Los Alamos, produced the first atomic bombs. It was led by General Leslie Groves. The first test took place in July 1945 at Trinity site. For 10 points, name this project.

In May 1937 this German airship burst into flames while docking at Lakehurst, New Jersey. A radio reporter famously cried, "Oh, the humanity!" Its lift came from hydrogen. For 10 points, name this disaster.

In April 1986 a reactor at this nuclear plant in Ukraine exploded during a safety test. The disaster spread radiation across Europe. The nearby town of Pripyat was abandoned. For 10 points, name this nuclear disaster.

This Spanish explorer landed in Florida in 1539 and crossed the southeastern United States. He was the first European to see the Mississippi River and was buried in it in 1542. For 10 points, name this conquistador.

This Italian navigator sailed for Henry VII of England in 1497 and reached the coast of Newfoundland. His son Sebastian also explored. His Italian name is Giovanni Caboto. For 10 points, name this man.

This 1494 agreement between Spain and Portugal divided newly discovered lands outside Europe along a line west of the Cape Verde Islands. Pope Alexander VI had earlier issued a similar bull. Portugal received Brazil as a result. For 10 points, name this treaty named for a Spanish town.

In 1854 miners at Ballarat in Victoria rebelled against license fees in this armed uprising. About two dozen miners and a few soldiers died. The rebels flew a flag with the Southern Cross. For 10 points, name this Australian event named for a wooden defensive barrier.

This English privateer was the second person to circumnavigate the globe and was knighted by Queen Elizabeth I aboard the Golden Hind. He raided Spanish ships and helped defeat the Armada in 1588. For 10 points, name this man.

In 1587 about 115 English settlers landed at this island off North Carolina, sponsored by Sir Walter Raleigh. When ships returned in 1590 everyone had vanished and the word "Croatoan" was carved on a post. For 10 points, name this lost colony.

This Australian outlaw wore homemade armor of iron plates in a final shootout at Glenrowan in 1880. His gang included his brother Dan and Steve Hart. He wrote the Jerilderie Letter and was hanged in Melbourne. For 10 points, name this bushranger.

parts: Which Aztec emperor welcomed Cortes in 1519?
Which president ruled Mexico for most of 1876 to 1911 before the Revolution?
Which 1810 cry of rebellion by a priest began the War of Independence?

q: Answer these questions about Canadian history.
parts: Which Ontario city is the capital of Canada?
Which 1759 battle on the Plains of Abraham gave Britain control of New France?
Which Canadian railway, completed in 1885, linked the east and west?

q: Answer these questions about Australia and New Zealand.
parts: Which British captain mapped Australia's east coast in 1770?
What was Australia originally used as by Britain, starting in 1788?
Which Maori meeting house treaty of 1840 did the Crown sign with chiefs?

q: Answer these questions about Antarctic and Arctic exploration.
parts: Which Norwegian was first to the South Pole?
Which American naval officer claimed to have reached the North Pole in 1909?
Which Norwegian scientist drifted across the Arctic in the ship Fram?

q: Answer these questions about Latin American leaders.
parts: Who led Cuba's revolution in 1959?
Which Argentine president founded the Justicialist Party?
Which Chilean general ruled from 1973 to 1990?

q: Answer these questions about nuclear history.
parts: In which Japanese city was the first atomic bomb used in war dropped?
Which Italian physicist built the first nuclear reactor in Chicago in 1942?
Which nuclear power plant in Pennsylvania had a partial meltdown in 1979?

q: Answer these questions about the voyages of discovery.
parts: Which English captain's ships were named Endeavour and Resolution?
Which Portuguese prince sponsored voyages down the African coast in the fifteenth century?
Which Portuguese navigator rounded the Cape of Good Hope in 1488?

q: Answer these questions about science and technology history.
parts: Which Scottish-born inventor patented the telephone in 1876?
Which American inventor founded Menlo Park laboratory and developed a practical light bulb?
Which Serbian-born inventor developed alternating-current motors and worked briefly with Edison?

q: In 1805 this Shoshone teenager helped the Corps of Discovery cross the Rocky Mountains, carrying her infant son Jean Baptiste. She had been captured years earlier by the Hidatsa. Her brother Cameahwait helped provide horses. For 10 points, name this woman who guided Lewis and Clark.

This city on Lake Texcoco was where Hernan Cortes met Montezuma. Its descendants include a city of more than nine million. For 10 points, name the modern capital of Mexico, built on the ruins of the Aztec capital.

The narrator of this novel opens by saying "Call me Ishmael" before signing onto a Nantucket-based voyage. A carpenter in this book fashions a replacement leg from whalebone for the captain, and the sailor Queequeg carves a coffin that later saves the narrator's life. The ship in this novel sails from Nantucket on a doomed hunt for a white sperm whale that took its captain's leg. For 10 points, name this novel by Herman Melville about Captain Ahab and the Pequod.

Nick Carraway narrates this novel and rents a small house next door to a mansion where lavish parties are held every weekend. A green light at the end of a dock across the bay symbolizes the longing of the title character for Daisy Buchanan. The title character is shot in his swimming pool by George Wilson. For 10 points, name this Jazz Age novel by F. Scott Fitzgerald.

In this novel the title character and the runaway slave Jim travel down the Mississippi River on a raft. The two are joined for a time by con men calling themselves the Duke and the King. The narrator decides to "go to hell" rather than turn in Jim, and the novel is a sequel to a book about a boy who whitewashed a fence. For 10 points, name this novel by Mark Twain.

Scout Finch narrates this novel set in Maycomb, Alabama, in the 1930s. Her father defends the Black man Tom Robinson against a false charge of assault, and her neighbor Boo Radley saves her and her brother Jem from Bob Ewell. For 10 points, name this novel by Harper Lee.

This author's poems include "Annabel Lee" and "The Bells," and he wrote a story in which a narrator is haunted by the "vulture eye" of an old man. In another of his stories, a detective named C. Auguste Dupin solves a crime in the Rue Morgue. His best-known poem features a talking bird that repeats "Nevermore." For 10 points, name this American author of "The Raven."

Holden Caulfield narrates this novel from a rest home after being expelled from Pencey Prep. Holden dislikes "phonies" and wishes to protect children from falling off a cliff in a field of rye. He takes his sister Phoebe to a carousel in Central Park. For 10 points, name this novel by J. D. Salinger.

This poet's collection of free verse grew through several editions after its 1855 publication, and it includes "Song of Myself." He also wrote an elegy for Abraham Lincoln that begins "When Lilacs Last in the Dooryard Bloom'd." Another of his poems begins "O Captain! My Captain!" For 10 points, name this author of Leaves of Grass.

This poet lived in Amherst, Massachusetts, and wrote about 1,800 poems, most of which were published only after her death. Her poems use dashes and slant rhyme and include "Because I could not stop for Death" and "I'm Nobody! Who are you?" For 10 points, name this reclusive American poet.

In this play, set during the Salem witch trials, John Proctor refuses to sign a confession because he will not give up his good name. Abigail Williams leads a group of girls who accuse townspeople of witchcraft. It was written as an allegory for McCarthyism. For 10 points, name this play by Arthur Miller.

George and Lennie are migrant farmhands who dream of owning a farm where Lennie can tend rabbits. Lennie accidentally kills Curley's wife, and George shoots his friend to spare him a worse fate. For 10 points, name this novella by John Steinbeck.

This novel follows the Joad family as they leave their Oklahoma farm during the Dust Bowl and travel to California on Route 66. Ma Joad holds the family together, and Tom Joad promises to be "in the way kids laugh when they're hungry." The novel ends with Rose of Sharon nursing a starving man. For 10 points, name this novel by John Steinbeck.

Walter Lee Younger wants to invest his father's life insurance money in a liquor store, while his sister Beneatha hopes to become a doctor. The family plans to move into the white neighborhood of Clybourne Park. For 10 points, name this play by Lorraine Hansberry, whose title comes from a Langston Hughes poem.

Janie Crawford has three marriages in this novel, the last to Tea Cake, whom she is forced to shoot during a hurricane aftermath when he becomes rabid. Janie tells her story to her friend Pheoby. For 10 points, name this novel set in Eatonville, Florida, by Zora Neale Hurston.

This leader of the Transcendentalist movement delivered the "American Scholar" address and wrote the essays "Nature" and "Self-Reliance." He urged readers to "trust thyself" and was a mentor to Henry David Thoreau. For 10 points, name this Concord essayist.

This author spent two years living in a cabin near a pond in Concord and wrote a book about it. He was jailed for refusing to pay a poll tax and later wrote an essay on civil disobedience. For 10 points, name this author of Walden.

The fisherman Santiago spends 84 days without a catch before hooking a giant marlin far out in the Gulf Stream. After a long struggle he lashes the fish to his boat, but sharks eat it on the way home. The boy Manolin cares for him. For 10 points, name this short novel by Ernest Hemingway.

The Stage Manager narrates this three-act play set in Grover's Corners, New Hampshire. Emily Webb dies in childbirth and is allowed to relive one day, her twelfth birthday. The play uses minimal scenery. For 10 points, name this play by Thornton Wilder.

Meg, Jo, Beth, and Amy March live in Concord during the Civil War while their father serves as a chaplain. Jo becomes a writer and marries Professor Bhaer, while Beth dies of scarlet fever. For 10 points, name this novel by Louisa May Alcott.

This poet wrote "Mending Wall," which contains the line "Good fences make good neighbors," and the poem "Birches." He recited "The Gift Outright" at the inauguration of John F. Kennedy. His collections include North of Boston and New Hampshire. For 10 points, name this poet of "The Road Not Taken."

The unnamed narrator of this novel lives in a basement lit by 1,369 light bulbs and works for Brother Jack's Brotherhood. Early on, he is made to fight in a battle royal and receives a scholarship to a Southern college. Its prologue describes how people refuse to see the narrator. For 10 points, name this novel by Ralph Ellison.

Sethe kills her two-year-old daughter to prevent her from being taken back into slavery, and the ghost of the child haunts her house at 124 Bluestone Road. Paul D arrives at the house and Denver lives there with her mother. For 10 points, name this novel by Toni Morrison.

Henry Fleming flees from his first battle but later becomes a hero as a flag bearer in this novel, set during the Civil War. The wound he is said to bear is a "red badge." For 10 points, name this novel by Stephen Crane.

In this dystopian novel, a mechanical hound hunts fugitives, and Captain Beatty taunts a fireman with quotations. Mildred is addicted to wall-sized television screens and overdoses on pills. The hero joins exiles who memorize books so they will survive, and the title is the temperature at which paper burns. For 10 points, name this novel by Ray Bradbury.

Blanche DuBois travels to New Orleans to stay with her sister Stella in this play. Her brother-in-law Stanley Kowalski eventually destroys her fragile hold on reality. The play begins when Blanche takes a trolley named Desire. For 10 points, name this play by Tennessee Williams.

This Missouri-born poet wrote the collection The Weary Blues and a long sequence called Montage of a Dream Deferred. He created the character Jesse B. Semple in newspaper columns and co-wrote the play Mule Bone with Zora Neale Hurston. For 10 points, name this American poet.

This author's Leatherstocking Tales feature the frontiersman Natty Bumppo, also known as Hawkeye. One of his novels is set during the French and Indian War and involves the Mingo Magua and the Mohican Chingachgook. For 10 points, name this author of The Last of the Mohicans.

Jake Barnes, rendered impotent by a war wound, travels to Pamplona for the running of the bulls in one novel by this author. Another of his novels follows the American ambulance driver Frederic Henry and the nurse Catherine Barkley during World War I. For 10 points, name this author of The Sun Also Rises and A Farewell to Arms.

Willy Loman is a traveling salesman who has lost his job and sees visions of his brother Ben in this play. His sons Biff and Happy fail to achieve his dreams, and his wife Linda says "attention must be paid." For 10 points, name this play by Arthur Miller.

Edna Pontellier abandons her family and learns to swim on Grand Isle in this novel, which was criticized when it appeared in 1899. After falling in love with Robert Lebrun, she walks into the Gulf of Mexico. For 10 points, name this novel by Kate Chopin.

One short story by this author features a man who sleeps for twenty years in the Catskill Mountains after drinking with strange men. Another story by this author features Ichabod Crane being chased by a headless horseman near Sleepy Hollow. For 10 points, name this author of "Rip Van Winkle."
Answer these questions about Nathaniel Hawthorne.
parts: Hester Prynne is forced to wear a scarlet "A" for adultery in which Hawthorne novel?
The minister Arthur Dimmesdale is the secret father of which child of Hester Prynne?
Hawthorne's novel The House of the Seven Gables is set in which Massachusetts town, famous for its 1692 witch trials?

q: Answer these questions about the author of Adventures of Huckleberry Finn.
parts: Which character created by this author whitewashes a fence and explores a cave with Becky Thatcher?
The author's real name was Samuel Clemens. What pen name comes from a riverboat term meaning two fathoms deep?
The author wrote a memoir titled Life on this river, about his years as a steamboat pilot; it flows through Hannibal, Missouri.

q: Answer these questions about Edgar Allan Poe.
parts: Which Poe poem features a visitor that says only "Nevermore"?
In which Poe story does the narrator hear a beating heart beneath the floorboards?
Poe's detective who solves crimes in The Murders in the Rue Morgue has which name?

q: Answer these questions about Harlem Renaissance writers.
parts: Which Harlem Renaissance author wrote the experimental book Cane?
Which poet wrote "Heritage" and "Incident"?
Which Jamaican-born poet wrote "If We Must Die" and the novel Home to Harlem?

q: Answer these questions about novels of the Great Depression and Dust Bowl.
parts: Which John Steinbeck novella features George and Lennie?
Which family travels west from Oklahoma in The Grapes of Wrath?
Which Steinbeck novel, set in the Salinas Valley, retells the story of Cain and Abel?

q: Answer these questions about two American poets, one a recluse and one a New York journalist.
parts: Which of the two poets wrote "Song of Myself"?
Dickinson spent most of her life in which Massachusetts town?
"O Captain! My Captain!" was written about the death of which president?

q: Answer these questions about American drama.
parts: Which Arthur Miller play is about the Salem witch trials?
Which Streetcar character says she has "always depended on the kindness of strangers"?
Which playwright wrote the dream-memory play The Glass Menagerie about Amanda Wingfield?

q: Answer these questions about Ernest Hemingway.
parts: Which Hemingway book is about the fisherman Santiago?
Which novel by Hemingway is set during the Spanish Civil War and follows the dynamiter Robert Jordan?
Hemingway's A Farewell to Arms is set during which war?

q: Two feuding families, the Montagues and Capulets, are at the center of this play set in Verona. The title lovers meet at a masked ball and are secretly married by Friar Laurence. A plan involving a sleeping potion goes wrong, and both lovers die. For 10 points, name this tragedy by William Shakespeare.

In this play the ghost of a murdered king appears to his son on the battlements of Elsinore. The prince feigns madness, stages a play within a play, and mistakenly kills Polonius. It contains the soliloquy "To be, or not to be." For 10 points, name this tragedy by William Shakespeare.

Three witches tell a Scottish general that he will become king, spurring him on to murder. His wife urges him on and later sleepwalks, trying to wash imaginary blood from her hands. Birnam Wood appears to move to Dunsinane Hill in this play. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare tragedy.

Elizabeth Bennet rejects a first proposal from Mister Darcy, in part because of his pride and because of lies told by George Wickham. Her sister Jane falls in love with Mister Bingley, and Lydia elopes with Wickham. For 10 points, name this novel by Jane Austen.

Ebenezer Scrooge is visited by the ghost of his dead partner, Jacob Marley, and then by three spirits representing past, present, and future. Scrooge's clerk, Bob Cratchit, has a sickly son named Tiny Tim. For 10 points, name this Charles Dickens novella.

Pip is helped by a secret benefactor after he meets an escaped convict named Abel Magwitch on the marshes. He later visits the eccentric Miss Havisham and falls in love with her ward Estella. For 10 points, name this novel by Charles Dickens.

This novel's title character becomes a governess at Thornfield Hall, where she falls in love with Mister Rochester. A mysterious laugh in the attic turns out to come from Rochester's first wife, Bertha Mason. For 10 points, name this novel by Charlotte Bronte.

A young scientist builds a creature from body parts and brings it to life in a laboratory. The creature, abandoned by its maker, learns language by watching a family and then seeks revenge. Mary Shelley wrote this novel as part of a ghost story contest. For 10 points, name this novel.

A group of boys stranded on an island elect Ralph as their leader, but Jack leads a rebellion. Piggy's glasses are used to start a signal fire, and Simon is killed during a frenzy. For 10 points, name this novel by William Golding.

Winston Smith works at the Ministry of Truth, rewriting history, and secretly begins a love affair with Julia. He is arrested and tortured in Room 101 by O'Brien. Big Brother watches the citizens of Oceania. For 10 points, name this dystopian novel by George Orwell.

The pig Squealer spreads propaganda, and the sheep chant "four legs good, two legs bad." Napoleon drives out his rival Snowball, and the workhorse Boxer is sold to a knacker after working himself to exhaustion on a windmill. A commandment is altered to say "but some animals are more equal than others." For 10 points, name this allegorical novella by George Orwell.

The hero of this Old English poem defeats the monster Grendel and Grendel's mother, then dies fighting a dragon as king of the Geats. The poem is set in Heorot, the hall of Hrothgar. For 10 points, name this epic poem.

A group of pilgrims tell stories to pass the time on a trip from the Tabard Inn to Canterbury. Characters include the Wife of Bath, the Miller, and the Pardoner. For 10 points, name this work in Middle English by Geoffrey Chaucer.

This Romantic poet wrote that poetry is "the spontaneous overflow of powerful feelings" in the preface to Lyrical Ballads. He also wrote "Tintern Abbey" and the poem about wandering "lonely as a cloud" and seeing daffodils. For 10 points, name this friend of Coleridge.

Heathcliff is brought to a house on the Yorkshire moors and falls in love with Catherine Earnshaw, who marries Edgar Linton instead. Nelly Dean narrates much of this novel. For 10 points, name this novel by Emily Bronte.

In this play Puck mistakenly puts a love potion on the eyes of Lysander, and Titania falls in love with Bottom, who has been given a donkey's head. Oberon and Titania quarrel over a changeling boy. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare comedy.

This epic poem begins by invoking a Heavenly Muse to sing of "man's first disobedience." It features Satan declaring "Better to reign in Hell than serve in Heaven" and ends with Adam and Eve leaving Eden. Written by a blind poet, it is in twelve books. For 10 points, name this epic by John Milton.

The title character in this satire visits the flying island of Laputa, where scientists neglect practical matters, and meets the immortal but miserable Struldbrugs. He ends up preferring the company of intelligent horses called Houyhnhnms to humans. The author also wrote "A Modest Proposal." For 10 points, name this satire by Jonathan Swift.

This author created a detective who lives at 221B Baker Street and is assisted by Doctor Watson. His villain Professor Moriarty fought the detective at the Reichenbach Falls. For 10 points, name this author of The Hound of the Baskervilles.

Jim Hawkins finds a map in the chest of Billy Bones and sails on the Hispaniola in search of buried loot. The cook Long John Silver turns out to be a pirate and the leader of a mutiny. For 10 points, name this adventure novel by Robert Louis Stevenson.

Algernon pretends to be named Ernest to attract Cecily, while Jack uses the same name to court Gwendolen. Lady Bracknell famously asks "A handbag?" on learning where Jack was found as a baby. For 10 points, name this play by Oscar Wilde.

Marlow narrates a journey up the Congo River to find the ivory trader Kurtz, whose last words are "The horror! The horror!" This novella is told on a boat on the Thames. For 10 points, name this work by Joseph Conrad.

Angel Clare abandons his bride after she confesses she bore a child outside of marriage; she is later hanged after murdering Alec. This novel is set in Wessex and is subtitled "A Pure Woman." For 10 points, name this novel by Thomas Hardy.

This Middle English poem begins when a green giant enters Camelot at New Year and proposes a beheading game. The hero is later tempted by the wife of Lord Bertilak. For 10 points, name this poem about a knight of King Arthur's court.

In this dystopia, babies are grown in hatcheries and conditioned to accept their castes, and the drug soma keeps citizens happy. John the Savage is brought from a reservation to London. For 10 points, name this novel by Aldous Huxley.

This modernist author's novels include Mrs Dalloway and To the Lighthouse, and her long essay argues that a woman needs money and a room of her own to write fiction. She was a member of the Bloomsbury Group. For 10 points, name this author of Orlando.

Bilbo Baggins is recruited by Gandalf to join a company of thirteen dwarves, including Thorin Oakenshield. He finds a ring in a cave while riddling with Gollum and helps recover treasure from Smaug. For 10 points, name this prequel to The Lord of the Rings by J. R. R. Tolkien.

This Romantic poet wrote the long satirical poem Don Juan and the autobiographical Childe Harold's Pilgrimage. He was described as "mad, bad, and dangerous to know" and died during the Greek War of Independence. For 10 points, name this poet.

In this play, Iago convinces the Moorish general that his wife Desdemona has been unfaithful, using a lost handkerchief as evidence. Cassio is demoted, and Roderigo is used as a pawn. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare tragedy.

Jonathan Harker travels to Transylvania to meet a count who is later shipped to England in boxes of earth. Abraham Van Helsing leads the hunt, and Mina Harker is menaced. For 10 points, name this vampire novel by Bram Stoker.
Answer these questions about William Shakespeare.
parts: Which tragedy features Iago and Desdemona?
Which comedy features the twins Viola and Sebastian in Illyria?
In which play does the title king divide his kingdom among his three daughters and go mad on the heath?

q: Answer these questions about the Bronte sisters.
parts: Which Charlotte Bronte novel features Mister Rochester?
Which Emily Bronte novel is set on the Yorkshire moors and features Heathcliff?
Which Bronte sister wrote Agnes Grey and The Tenant of Wildfell Hall?

q: Answer these questions about Charles Dickens.
parts: Which Dickens novella features Ebenezer Scrooge?
Which Dickens novel features the orphan who asks for more gruel and falls in with the Artful Dodger?
In A Tale of Two Cities, which two cities are the settings?

q: Answer these questions about dystopian novels.
parts: Which author wrote Nineteen Eighty-Four?
Which Huxley novel features the drug soma?
Which dystopian novel by Yevgeny Zamyatin influenced both Orwell and Huxley?

q: Answer these questions about Jane Austen.
parts: Which Austen novel features the poor relation Fanny Price?
Which Austen heroine meddles in matchmaking in Highbury?
Which Austen novel is a parody of Gothic fiction and features Catherine Morland?

q: Answer these questions about Romantic poets.
parts: Which poet wrote about daffodils and "Tintern Abbey"?
Which Romantic poet wrote the long poem "Endymion," which begins "A thing of beauty is a joy forever"?
Which poet wrote "Ozymandias" and "Ode to the West Wind"?

q: Answer these questions about medieval English literature.
parts: Which Old English epic features the monster Grendel?
Sir Gawain serves which legendary king?
In Chaucer's long poem about Troilus, he loves which Trojan woman?

q: Answer these questions about adventure and mystery stories.
parts: Which detective lives at 221B Baker Street?
Which Gothic novella features a London doctor whose potion transforms him into a violent alter ego?
Which author wrote Treasure Island?

q: A deluded minor nobleman reads so many chivalric romances that he sets out as a knight-errant with a farmer named Sancho Panza as his squire. He attacks windmills he believes to be giants and calls a peasant woman, Dulcinea, his lady. For 10 points, name this novel by Miguel de Cervantes.

In this poem the narrator is guided by Virgil through nine circles of a place in which sinners are punished according to their sins. Its inscription over the gate says "Abandon all hope, ye who enter here." The poet ends up meeting the traitors Judas, Brutus, and Cassius in the ninth circle. For 10 points, name this first part of the Divine Comedy by Dante.

The ex-convict Jean Valjean is hunted for decades by the policeman Javert in this novel, which climaxes at a barricade during the June Rebellion of 1832. Valjean adopts the orphan Cosette, who falls in love with Marius. For 10 points, name this novel by Victor Hugo.

A pilot stranded in the Sahara meets a small boy who has traveled from an asteroid and who cares for a single rose. He also befriends a fox, who teaches him that "what is essential is invisible to the eye." For 10 points, name this novella by Antoine de Saint-Exupery.

After the murder of an old pawnbroker, a former student named Raskolnikov is slowly worn down by guilt and by the detective Porfiry Petrovich. He confesses at the urging of the pious Sonya. For 10 points, name this novel by Fyodor Dostoevsky.

Pierre Bezukhov fights a duel with Dolokhov and later befriends the peasant Platon Karataev as a prisoner of the French. Prince Andrei is wounded at Austerlitz, and Natasha nearly elopes with Anatole Kuragin. The story covers the Napoleonic wars in Russia. For 10 points, name this very long novel by Leo Tolstoy.

Gregor Samsa wakes up to discover he has been turned into a giant insect. His family becomes increasingly resentful, and he dies after his father throws apples at him. For 10 points, name this novella by Franz Kafka.

The title scholar makes a pact with the devil Mephistopheles, and he falls in love with the young Gretchen. Dissatisfied with the limits of human knowledge, he wagers that he will never say to a moment "Stay, you are so beautiful." For 10 points, name this dramatic poem by Johann Wolfgang von Goethe.

The title character in this novel leaves her husband Karenin for Count Vronsky and throws herself under a train. A parallel plot follows the landowner Konstantin Levin and his courtship of Kitty. For 10 points, name this novel by Leo Tolstoy.

Nora Helmer forges a signature to save her husband's life, and then leaves him at the end of this play. Torvald calls her his "little squirrel," and she slams the door as she walks out. For 10 points, name this play by Henrik Ibsen.

Meursault attends his mother's funeral without crying and later shoots an Arab on a beach in Algiers. He is sentenced to death partly because of his apparent indifference. For 10 points, name this novel by Albert Camus.

A cadet with a large nose writes love letters for the handsome Christian to the beautiful Roxane. This play by Edmond Rostand ends with the hero dying while reciting a poem. For 10 points, name this title poet-swordsman.

Dr. Pangloss insists that this is "the best of all possible worlds" despite earthquakes and Inquisition burnings. The young hero is expelled from the castle of Baron Thunder-ten-tronckh for kissing Cunegonde. At the end, he decides "we must cultivate our garden." For 10 points, name this satire by Voltaire.

Edmond Dantes is imprisoned in the Chateau d'If after being falsely accused of treason. After escaping with the help of the Abbe Faria, he finds a hidden treasure and takes revenge on Danglars, Fernand, and Villefort. For 10 points, name this novel by Alexandre Dumas.

Charles Bovary's wife, Emma, has affairs with Rodolphe and Leon and runs up debts with the merchant Lheureux. She eventually poisons herself with arsenic. For 10 points, name this realist novel by Gustave Flaubert.

The monk Alyosha, the intellectual Ivan, and the sensualist Dmitri are three sons of the lecherous Fyodor Pavlovich, who is murdered. In this novel the "Grand Inquisitor" is a poem told by Ivan. For 10 points, name this last novel by Fyodor Dostoevsky.

The swindler Chichikov travels around Russia buying up serfs who have died but are still counted on tax rolls. This unfinished novel by Nikolai Gogol is subtitled "A Poem." For 10 points, name this work whose title refers to deceased serfs.

This Danish author wrote fairy tales including "The Ugly Duckling," "The Snow Queen," and "The Emperor's New Clothes." He also wrote about a mermaid who gives up her voice to gain legs. For 10 points, name this author.

In this play by a French dramatist, the title religious hypocrite is welcomed into the home of Orgon, who wants him to marry his daughter. Elmire exposes the impostor by hiding her husband under a table. For 10 points, name this comedy by Moliere.

Seven young women and three young men flee plague-stricken Florence to a villa in this work, where each tells a story every day for ten days. For 10 points, name this collection of one hundred tales by Giovanni Boccaccio.

Paul Baumer narrates this novel about a group of German schoolboys who enlist after a patriotic speech by their teacher, Kantorek. Paul is killed on a day when the army report says there was nothing new. For 10 points, name this World War I novel by Erich Maria Remarque.

Josef K. is arrested one morning without being told what he is charged with. He is led to a quarry and killed "like a dog" after dealing with a nearly inaccessible court. For 10 points, name this unfinished novel by Franz Kafka.

This novel in verse follows a bored aristocrat who rejects the love of Tatyana and later kills his friend Lensky in a duel. The title character, a dandy, later regrets his rejection when she is married. For 10 points, name this work by Alexander Pushkin.

The Gaev family loses its estate to the businessman Lopakhin, who has it cut down for summer cottages. The sound of an axe is heard as the family leaves. For 10 points, name this play by Anton Chekhov.

A carpenter carves a puppet from a piece of wood, and it comes to life. Whenever the puppet lies, his nose grows longer, and he is swallowed by a giant whale. For 10 points, name this character, the creation of Carlo Collodi.

A man named Govinda accompanies a young Brahmin on his journey, but then the hero meets the Buddha and decides to find his own path. He eventually becomes a ferryman and learns from a river. For 10 points, name this novel by Hermann Hesse.

This multi-volume work begins with the narrator dipping a madeleine into tea, which triggers memories of Combray. It follows Swann's love for Odette and the narrator's love for Albertine. For 10 points, name this work by Marcel Proust.

A young man falls in love with Lotte, who is engaged to Albert, and he shoots himself with a pistol borrowed from Albert. This novel in letters brought its young author fame and inspired a wave of suicides. For 10 points, name this work by Goethe.

This poet wrote a collection of poems called "Flowers of Evil" and translated Edgar Allan Poe into French. He also wrote the poem "Correspondances" and introduced the figure of the flaneur. For 10 points, name this French poet.

The title doctor falls in love with Lara, who is also loved by Komarovsky, and writes poems during the Russian Revolution. The novel's publication was suppressed in the Soviet Union, and its author won the Nobel Prize in 1958. For 10 points, name this novel by Boris Pasternak.

q: Okonkwo, a wrestler and farmer in the village of Umuofia, kills a messenger and accidentally kills a clansman, leading to his exile. When he returns, missionaries have transformed his community, and he hangs himself. For 10 points, name this novel by Chinua Achebe.

The Buendia family lives in the town of Macondo, which is founded by Jose Arcadio Buendia. Colonel Aureliano Buendia fights in civil wars, and the last of the family reads Melquiades's parchments as the town is blown away. For 10 points, name this novel by Gabriel Garcia Marquez.

A woman tells a story every night to a king who has been executing his brides after one night. She saves herself by leaving each tale unfinished at dawn. Stories in this collection include "Aladdin" and "Sinbad the Sailor." For 10 points, name this collection.

This epic poem begins with an invocation of the Muse and follows a king of Ithaca who spends ten years trying to return home after the Trojan War. He blinds the Cyclops Polyphemus and listens to the Sirens tied to a mast. For 10 points, name this epic attributed to Homer.

This epic begins with the wrath of a Greek hero, who withdraws from battle after a quarrel with Agamemnon. His friend Patroclus is killed wearing his armor, and he kills Hector in revenge. For 10 points, name this epic attributed to Homer about the Trojan War.

Dasaratha's wife Kaikeyi demands that his eldest son be exiled for fourteen years. Rama's brother Lakshmana accompanies him, and Hanuman leaps over the sea to find the kidnapped Sita in Lanka. It is traditionally ascribed to Valmiki. For 10 points, name this Sanskrit epic attributed to Valmiki.

This enormous Sanskrit epic is about a war between the Pandavas and the Kauravas, and includes a dialogue between Arjuna and Krishna on the battlefield of Kurukshetra. For 10 points, name this epic, which contains the Bhagavad Gita.

Often called the world's first novel, this work by Murasaki Shikibu follows a prince of the Heian court and his many romances. Written in the early eleventh century, it also follows his son Kaoru. For 10 points, name this Japanese work whose title character is "shining."

This author renounced his knighthood in 1919 after the Amritsar massacre. He wrote the novel The Home and the World and the songs that became the national anthems of India and Bangladesh. He won the 1913 Nobel Prize for a collection of "Song Offerings." For 10 points, name this author.

This poet served as consul in Burma and as ambassador to France under Salvador Allende. He lived at Isla Negra and appears as a character in the film Il Postino. He wrote the collection Residence on Earth and the epic Canto General. For 10 points, name this poet.
This Nigerian author was the first African to win the Nobel Prize in Literature, in 1986. His plays include Death and the King's Horseman and A Dance of the Forests. For 10 points, name this author.

This Argentine writer's short stories include "The Garden of Forking Paths," "The Library of Babel," and "The Aleph." His story collections include Ficciones and Labyrinths, and he was blind in his later years. For 10 points, name this author.

In this Chinese novel, a monk named Tripitaka travels to India to obtain Buddhist scriptures, accompanied by Pigsy, Sandy, and a monkey who can transform in seventy-two ways. For 10 points, name this novel, whose Monkey King is Sun Wukong.

This Qing dynasty novel follows the decline of the Jia family and the love triangle among Jia Baoyu, Lin Daiyu, and Xue Baochai. Cao Xueqin wrote the first eighty chapters. For 10 points, name this classic of Chinese literature, also known as The Story of the Stone.

Saleem Sinai is born at the stroke of midnight on the day India becomes independent and has telepathic powers connecting him to other children born in that hour. For 10 points, name this novel by Salman Rushdie.

This Mesopotamian epic follows a king of Uruk and his friend Enkidu, who is created by the gods. After Enkidu's death, the hero seeks immortality from Utnapishtim, a survivor of a flood. For 10 points, name this epic.

The Trojan Aeneas flees the burning city and has a tragic affair with the queen of Carthage, Dido. He then travels to Italy, where his descendants will found Rome. For 10 points, name this Latin epic by Virgil.

The seer Tiresias tells the king that he himself is the cause of a plague. A shepherd from Corinth reveals that the king was left on a mountain as a baby, after solving the riddle of the Sphinx. Jocasta hangs herself, and the king puts out his own eyes. For 10 points, name this play by Sophocles.

In this tragedy, the title princess of Colchis kills her own children to take revenge on her husband Jason, who plans to marry Glauce. She then escapes in a chariot drawn by dragons. For 10 points, name this play by Euripides.

In this Chilean novel, the Trueba family is led by Esteban and his wife Clara, who has clairvoyant powers. The granddaughter Alba is tortured after a military coup. For 10 points, name this first novel by Isabel Allende.

This Egyptian author's novels include Midaq Alley and the Cairo Trilogy, which follows the family of Al-Sayyid Ahmad Abd al-Jawad. He won the 1988 Nobel Prize in Literature. For 10 points, name this author.

This Japanese author wrote Norwegian Wood, Kafka on the Shore, and The Wind-Up Bird Chronicle. His novels blend realism with magic and often feature cats, wells, and jazz. For 10 points, name this author.
This Persian epic by Ferdowsi recounts the history of Persian kings, including the hero Rostam, who unknowingly kills his own son Sohrab. For 10 points, name this national epic of Iran.

This author wrote the Masnavi and the Diwan of Shams of Tabriz. A Persian poet and Sufi mystic, he founded the Mevlevi order, known for whirling dervishes. For 10 points, name this thirteenth-century poet.
In this South African novel, Reverend Stephen Kumalo travels to Johannesburg to search for his son Absalom, who has killed a white man. For 10 points, name this novel by Alan Paton.

In this black-and-white work, the author is sent to school in Vienna as a teenager and later returns home to marry. A young girl wears a headscarf to school after the fall of the Shah. Its author describes growing up in Iran during the Islamic Revolution and the Iran-Iraq War. For 10 points, name this graphic memoir by Marjane Satrapi.

Women of Athens and Sparta go on a sex strike to force their husbands to end the Peloponnesian War. The heroine leads the women who seize the Acropolis, and the men eventually give in. For 10 points, name this comedy by Aristophanes.

This Roman poet, who was exiled to Tomis by Augustus, wrote the Art of Love and a poem of fifteen books, which retells myths of transformations from creation to the deification of Julius Caesar. For 10 points, name this author of Metamorphoses.
A young man named Juan Preciado goes to the town of Comala to look for his father, only to find a town of whispering ghosts. For 10 points, name this novel by Mexican author Juan Rulfo.
This Lebanese-American writer's book of twenty-six prose poems is spoken by Almustafa, who is leaving the city of Orphalese after twelve years. For 10 points, name this author of The Prophet.

In this dystopian novel, Offred is a handmaid in the Republic of Gilead. Her role is to bear children for the Commander and his wife Serena Joy. For 10 points, name this novel by Canadian author Margaret Atwood.

q: A pig named Wilbur is saved from slaughter when a barn spider spins words like "SOME PIG" in her web. The girl Fern befriends the pig, and the rat Templeton helps the spider. For 10 points, name this children's novel by E. B. White.

An orphan raised by the Dursleys learns on his eleventh birthday that he is a wizard and is sent to Hogwarts. His friends Ron and Hermione help him fight the dark wizard Voldemort, who gave him a lightning-shaped scar. For 10 points, name this series by J. K. Rowling.

Four siblings named Peter, Susan, Edmund, and Lucy enter a magical land through a wardrobe. They help the lion Aslan defeat the White Witch, who has made it always winter but never Christmas. For 10 points, name this fantasy series by C. S. Lewis.

A girl follows a talking White Rabbit down a hole and encounters a Cheshire Cat, a Mad Hatter, and a Queen who says "Off with her head." For 10 points, name this novel by Lewis Carroll, which was followed by a sequel about a looking glass.

This author wrote about a mischievous feline in a tall striped hat and about a Grinch who steals Christmas. His real name was Theodor Geisel, and he also wrote Green Eggs and Ham. For 10 points, name this children's author.

Meg Murry travels through a tesseract with her brother Charles Wallace to rescue her father from the evil force IT. Three strange guides named Whatsit, Who, and Which help the children. For 10 points, name this novel by Madeleine L'Engle.
Jonas lives in a community without pain or color and is chosen as the Receiver of Memory. He later runs away with a baby named Gabriel. For 10 points, name this dystopian novel by Lois Lowry.

In this novel, the desert planet Arrakis is the only source of the spice melange. Paul Atreides becomes the leader of the Fremen and is called Muad'Dib. The Bene Gesserit and the Harkonnens oppose his house. For 10 points, name this science-fiction novel by Frank Herbert.

Arthur Dent is saved from the destruction of Earth by his friend Ford Prefect, who is writing an entry for a guidebook. The answer to the ultimate question of life, the universe, and everything is 42. For 10 points, name this comic science-fiction novel by Douglas Adams.

A boy genius named Andrew Wiggin is trained at Battle School to fight an alien race called the Formics, or buggers. His sister Valentine and his brother Peter are also very intelligent. For 10 points, name this novel by Orson Scott Card.

This form of Japanese poetry normally contains seventeen syllables, arranged in three lines of five, seven, and five. Matsuo Basho was a master of this form, which usually refers to a season. For 10 points, name this poetic form.
This poem has fourteen lines. The Petrarchan form is divided into an octave and a sestet, while the Shakespearean form ends in a rhyming couplet. For 10 points, name this poetic form.

Edward Lear popularized this form in his Book of Nonsense, and the poet Ogden Nash wrote many. Its first, second, and fifth lines rhyme and are longer than its third and fourth. It is often bawdy and begins with a line such as "There once was a man from Nantucket." For 10 points, name this form.

A Jewish girl hides in the Secret Annex above her father's business in Amsterdam with her family and four others. She is given a red-checked book on her thirteenth birthday. For 10 points, name this diary kept from 1942 to 1944 by Anne Frank.

This memoir by an escaped slave describes his time with the cruel overseer Covey and his fight with him. The author later became an abolitionist and editor of The North Star. For 10 points, name this autobiography by Frederick Douglass.

This memoir recounts the author's time in Auschwitz and Buchenwald with his father Shlomo, whom he loses shortly before liberation. The author won the 1986 Nobel Peace Prize. For 10 points, name this memoir by Elie Wiesel.
